newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Flies send Manila's "Dirty Harry" off to new war.
newsitem.headline: Flies send Manila's "Dirty Harry" off to new war.

text.p: A Philippine mayor who shut hundreds of bars in an effort to rid Manila of prostitutes is on the warpath again -- against flies and cockroaches.
Blaming them for the death of seven people in a cholera outbreak in the capital, Manila Mayor Alfredo Lim on Saturday offered cash to residents who capture the insects.
Scores of residents queued up at the poor Paco district to be paid for capturing nearly 2,000 flies and cockroaches which they had brought in plastic bags.
Officials paid them 15 pesos (about six U.S. cents) for each bag of 10 flies or 10 cockroaches which were later burned.
Lim said he would pay bigger money -- 20 centavos (about eight cents) -- for a rat.
More than 300 people have been hospitalised with cholera caused, officials said, by contaminated water and food.

Lim earned the label "Dirty Harry" -- after a trigger-happy Hollywood character played by American actor Clint Eastwood -- in the Manila press for his tough methods in dealing with criminals while he was Manila's police chief.
Elected mayor in 1992, he won praise from the Roman Catholic church for closing more than 300 bars he said were acting as fronts for prostitution in Manila's "red light" district.
